title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a notation sheet that opens the next block of notes on Chow groups and Lefschetz-type questions. It comes after the tables on the previous page comparing a variety X with a hyperplane section Y, and the maps given by powers of the hyperplane class.

Setting: X is a smooth projective variety.

Cohomology:
- H^*(X) is classical cohomology.
- P^*(X) is its primitive part. With L the hyperplane class, this is the kernel of L^{n-2i+1} on H^{2i}, or more generally on H^k.
- A marginal note says one may also put in coefficients.

Cycles:
- A^*(X) = A^*_r(X) is the Chow ring (rational equivalence).
- N^*(X) = A^*_a(X) is the ring of cycles modulo algebraic equivalence.
- J^*(X) = A^*_r(X)^a is the kernel: cycles algebraically equivalent to zero, taken modulo rational equivalence.
- This gives the exact sequence 0 → J^*(X) → A^*(X) → N^*(X) → 0.

Primitive parts:
- M^*(X) is the primitive part of N^*(X). This is meaningful if hard Lefschetz holds for L acting on N, which is a Lefschetz-type standard conjecture for algebraic equivalence.
- I^*(X) is the primitive part of J^*(X).
- The next page conjectures that the groups A^i_r(X)^a are abelian varieties. In that picture, I^i would be a 'primitive' abelian subvariety, the cycle-theoretic analogue of the primitive part of the intermediate Jacobian.

The N.B. reads: 'Il ne me semble pas qu'il y ait une définition raisonnable de la "partie primitive" de A(X)'. Grothendieck observes that the full Chow ring has no reasonable primitive part. The implicit reason is that the extension 0→J→A→N→0 has no canonical splitting compatible with L. A Lefschetz decomposition on A^* would need such a splitting, or a filtration.

The page serves the programme of the surrounding notes: Lefschetz-type theorems for Chow groups (X versus its hyperplane section Y, and the maps E^k given by powers of the hyperplane class), and the structure of algebraically trivial cycles.
errors: No mathematical claim is made on this page beyond definitions. The definitions of M^* and I^* as 'primitive parts' implicitly presuppose Lefschetz-type properties of cup-product with L on N^* and J^*, which are conjectural; the general case is still open.

The adjacent page's hope that A^i_r(X)^a are abelian varieties is false in general (Mumford 1968/69 on 0-cycles of surfaces with p_g>0; Griffiths 1969). That bears on the intended meaning of I^*(X), but is not an error on this page itself.

ideas.what: Primitive parts of cycle groups modulo algebraic equivalence (M^*) and of algebraically trivial cycle classes modulo rational equivalence (I^*)
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz (primitive) decomposition on cycle groups; motivic hard Lefschetz; for J^*, compare Künnemann's Lefschetz decomposition for Chow motives of abelian varieties and Bloch–Beilinson/Murre graded pieces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (standard conjectures, ~1968–69) for numerical/homological equivalence; Künnemann (1990s) for Chow motives of abelian varieties
ideas.where_published: 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968, publ. 1969) treats primitive decomposition for algebraic cycles modulo homological/numerical equivalence; the version for J^* is not, as far as I know, published

ideas.what: Remark that the full Chow ring has no reasonable primitive part because 0→J→A→N→0 does not split canonically
ideas.modern_name: Need for a (conjectural) Bloch–Beilinson / Murre filtration or Chow–Künneth decomposition to define Lefschetz decompositions on Chow groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bloch, Beilinson (1980s), Murre (1993); Beauville decomposition for abelian varieties (1986)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly notes that the Chow ring itself admits no natural primitive decomposition. He separates the problem into the algebraic-equivalence quotient N^* and the algebraically trivial part J^*, each of which should carry one. This foreshadows the later practice of getting Lefschetz decompositions on Chow groups only via a filtration or splitting (Beauville, Künnemann, Murre). It is a perceptive remark but not a new result.
missed.quote: Il ne me semble pas qu'il y ait une définition raisonnable de la "partie primitive" de A(X)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents that Grothendieck was aware, circa 1965–71, that Lefschetz theory on Chow groups requires splitting the rational/algebraic-equivalence extension. That anticipates the motivic-filtration viewpoint, though the later literature reached it independently.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a pure notation page. The only notable item is the N.B. observing that the Chow ring has no reasonable primitive part, a perceptive anticipation of later filtration-based approaches. It is not a result, and specialists would find it natural.
transcription_corrections: 'Je ne semble pas qu'il y ait' should read 'Il ne me semble pas qu'il y ait'.
In the N.B. the object is written as script A(X), without an asterisk, i.e. the Chow ring A^*(X).
The bracket note at right reads 'on peut mettre des coeff.' and refers to both H^* and P^*.
